summary.en: Middle English abandounen (English verb attested in the 14th century) was borrowed from Anglo-French abanduner, derived from abandun and a bandun, referring to power or disposal. Continental Old French à bandon likewise concerns disposal; abandonner is derived from abandon (CNRTL records releasing a rein around 1100 and leaving entirely from the 12th century). This supports the development toward relinquish/give up. It is not historically ban + donner. Bandon belongs to a Germanic command/jurisdiction background; this is not the author’s modern segmentation. Bandon itself means power/authority, not release. The displayed pathway is a semantic abstraction, not a strict chronology of first attestations.

claim.en: English ban (verb) continues Old English bannan, a Germanic proclamation/command verb; Middle English prohibitive senses reflect Norse influence, with later French/Latin influence. The English noun partly derives from the verb and partly from Anglo-French. French ban /bɑ̃/ is a masculine noun of Old Low Franconian origin: public proclamation, feudal summons/jurisdiction, banns, and exclusion in expressions such as mettre au ban. It is not the ordinary French verb “to prohibit” (interdire); the old note’s French ban v. 禁止 is corrected. This distinction does not cancel the independently proposed English ban ↔ 甭 candidate.
claim.zh-Hans: 英语动词 ban 承自古英语 bannan，属于日耳曼语宣告／命令词族；中古英语禁止等义受古诺斯语影响，后又受法语／拉丁语影响。英语名词部分来自动词，部分借自盎格鲁法语。法语 ban /bɑ̃/ 为阳性名词，源于古低地法兰克语，涉及公告、封建征召／管辖、婚姻公告及 mettre au ban 等排斥用语；它不是通常表示“禁止”的法语动词（interdire）。旧笔记“法语 ban v. 禁止”已纠正，这不取消独立的英语 ban ↔ 甭 候选。

claim.en: English banal is borrowed from French (Merriam-Webster: first known English use 1825). CNRTL traces French banal to feudal ban plus -al, with bannel attested in 1247 and the very common/unoriginal sense in 1798. Merriam-Webster describes a Medieval Latin bannalis route for Old French bannel. Both accounts connect seigneurial jurisdiction and shared-use facilities with the later commonplace sense. Neither derives it from Chinese. Ban and banal are separately evaluated observations, but their related European histories must be deduplicated in any family-based experiment.
claim.zh-Hans: 英语 banal 借自法语（Merriam-Webster 记英语首见1825年）。CNRTL 将法语 banal 分析为封建法 ban 加 -al，记1247年 bannel 及1798年的极普通／无新意义；Merriam-Webster 则通过中古拉丁语 bannalis 解释古法语 bannel。两者均联系领主管辖、共同使用设施与后来的平常义，不从汉语倒推词史。ban 和 banal 的观察独立评价，但欧洲词史相关，实验按词源家族去重。

claim.en: English ban ↔ 甭 béng: Phonetic-Semantic Candidate; semantic strength moderate; overall confidence Low; Historical Relation: Not claimed. The overlap is contextual DON’T / DO NOT / PROHIBIT. English ban often means formal prohibition; 甭 commonly means no need/do not and need not prohibit. English /bæn/ and béng show an author-observed labial onset and loose rhyme resemblance, not homophony: Pinyin b is unaspirated /p/, English b is /b/, final /n/ versus /ŋ/, vowels and tone differ.
claim.zh-Hans: 英语 ban ↔ 甭 béng：Phonetic-Semantic Candidate；语义强度 moderate，整体置信度 Low；Historical Relation: Not claimed。交点限于语境中的 DON’T / DO NOT / PROHIBIT。ban 常表正式禁止，“甭”常表不用／不必／不要，不总是禁止。/bæn/ 与 béng 的双唇起音及宽泛韵部近似仅为作者观察，并非同音：拼音 b 为不送气 /p/，英语 b 为 /b/，韵尾 /n/ 与 /ŋ/、元音和声调有别。

claim.en: banal ↔ 般 bān / 一般: Phonetic-Semantic Candidate; semantic strength moderate; overall confidence Low; Historical Relation: Not claimed. The semantic anchor is the word 一般 in its ordinary/common sense, not an assertion that isolated 般 always means ordinary. Modern banal often adds a negative sense of unoriginal or trite that 一般 need not carry. French /ba.nal/ permits a partial ban- versus bān comparison; English pronunciations vary. Unmatched /al/, vowels, voicing and Mandarin tone remain limitations.
claim.zh-Hans: banal ↔ 般 bān / 一般：Phonetic-Semantic Candidate；语义强度 moderate，整体置信度 Low；Historical Relation: Not claimed。语义依据是“一般”的普通／通常义，不主张单字“般”总有普通义。现代 banal 常含陈腐、无新意的贬义，“一般”未必如此。法语 /ba.nal/ 可与 bān 作局部 ban- 音近观察；英语有多种读法。未对应的 /al/、元音、清浊与汉语声调仍是限制。

claim.en: Bandon means POWER/AUTHORITY; disposal belongs to the relational phrase à bandon. Modern 办/辦 means handle/manage, prepare or deal with. 说文新附 glosses 辦 as exert effort (致力), not authority. Thus bandon ↔ 办 is a limited control/handling association: Low semantic fit for POWER/AUTHORITY, Medium only for a contextual handling/disposal comparison. It is not an exact root translation. 权柄 is the stronger meaning-first support for authority regardless of its sound.
claim.zh-Hans: bandon 的核心是 POWER/AUTHORITY；任其处置关系属于 à bandon。现代办／辦为处理、办理、筹备等；《说文新附》释辦为致力，不是权力。因此 bandon ↔ 办仅保留为支配／办理的有限联系：对权力本义语义适配 Low，只有在处理／处置语境比较时为 Medium，不是词根的精确译词。权柄是更合适的权力义支持，其声音不决定选择。

semantic_evaluation.en: Bandon means POWER/AUTHORITY; disposal belongs to the relational phrase à bandon. Modern 办/辦 means handle/manage, prepare or deal with. 说文新附 glosses 辦 as exert effort (致力), not authority. Thus bandon ↔ 办 is a limited control/handling association: Low semantic fit for POWER/AUTHORITY, Medium only for a contextual handling/disposal comparison. It is not an exact root translation. 权柄 is the stronger meaning-first support for authority regardless of its sound.

independent_observations.en: abash ↔ 怕 pà (medial b ↔ p) and bash ↔ 拍 pāi (initial b ↔ p) are two other separately identified Candidate observations. Sharing b-p-m-f does not make them prove each other or bandon ↔ 办. Statistical independence requires etymological-family review; count related derivatives once.
independent_observations.zh-Hans: abash ↔ 怕 pà（词中 b ↔ p）与 bash ↔ 拍 pāi（词首 b ↔ p）是另外两个分别记录的 Candidate 观察。共享 b-p-m-f 不使它们互相证明，也不证明 bandon ↔ 办；统计独立性仍需词源家族核验，同源派生须去重。

note.en: Dialect & Diachronic Chinese Evidence is a separate evidence track. Record dialect/location/date and transcription separately from Middle Chinese or Old Chinese reconstructions, with named sources and reconstruction systems. Modern dialects are not frozen copies of ancient Chinese. No dialect or reconstructed pronunciation is used to raise this candidate’s grade; these comparisons remain pending.
note.zh-Hans: Dialect & Diachronic Chinese Evidence｜汉语方言与历时音韵证据独立记录。方言须注明地点、年代与转写；中古音／上古音须注明来源与重构体系，不能混用。现代方言不是古汉语的冻结复制品。本候选未以方言或重构音提高等级，相关比较待核验。
